literal: Emperor Xiaozhuang bore the taboo name Ziyou; he was the third son of Prince of Pengcheng Rong; his mother was Consort Li.
idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhuang bore the taboo name Ziyou. He was the third son of Prince of Pengcheng Rong; his mother was Consort Li.

literal: At the beginning of Suzong's reign, because Rong had merit in guarding and supporting at Luyang, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Wucheng, state-founding.
idiomatic: Early in Suzong's reign, because Rong had merit guarding and supporting at Luyang, Ziyou was enfeoffed as state-founding Duke of Wucheng.

literal: In youth he attended Suzong in study within the forbidden quarters.
idiomatic: As a boy he studied with Suzong inside the palace.

literal: When grown, his spirit and bearing were elegant and wise, and his appearance very handsome.
idiomatic: When he came of age his bearing was elegant and keen, and his looks strikingly fine.

literal: He was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, colonel of the city gates, and concurrently Attendant at the Yellow Gate; he was greatly favored and trusted by Suzong and held long duty in the inner palace.
idiomatic: He was made vice director of the secretariat, colonel of the city gates, and concurrently attendant at the yellow gate; Suzong favored and trusted him deeply, and he kept long watches in the inner palace.

literal: He was transferred to scattered cavalier attendant and censor-in-chief.
idiomatic: He was transferred to scattered cavalier attendant and censor-in-chief.

literal: Eighth month of the second year of Xiaochang: he was advanced to Prince of Changle.
idiomatic: In the eighth month of the second year of Xiaochang he was advanced to prince of Changle.

literal: He was transferred to attendant-in-ordinary and general of the central army.
idiomatic: He was transferred to attendant-in-ordinary and general of the central army.

literal: Tenth month of the third year: because of the affair of his elder brother Prince of Pengcheng Xu, he was transferred to general of the guard, grand master of splendid carriages with golden seal and purple cord, and director of the secretariat—in truth he was being sent out.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of the third year, because of his elder brother Prince of Pengcheng Xu, he was transferred to general of the guard, grand master of splendid carriages with golden seal and purple cord, and director of the secretariat—a real demotion in all but name.

literal: When spring of the second month of the first year of Wutai came, Suzong died; Grand Commander Erzhu Rong was marching on the capital, plotting to depose and install.
idiomatic: In spring of the second month of the first year of Wutai, Suzong died. Grand Commander Erzhu Rong was marching on the capital with plans to depose and enthrone.

literal: Because the imperial house had loyal merit and he also enjoyed the people's regard, Rong secretly communicated with him; Rong then led his host to answer the summons.
idiomatic: Because the house had shown loyal merit and he enjoyed popular regard, Rong secretly treated with him; Rong then led his troops to answer the call.

literal: Fourth month, day bingchen: the Emperor and his brothers crossed the Yellow River north by night;
idiomatic: On bingchen day in the fourth month the emperor and his brothers crossed the Yellow River northward by night;

literal: day dingyou: he met Rong at Heyin.
idiomatic: on dingyou day he met Rong at Heyin.

literal: day wuxu: he crossed the river south and took the imperial throne.
idiomatic: On wuxu day he crossed south and took the throne.

literal: His elder brother Prince of Pengcheng Xu was made Prince Without Superior; his younger brother Zizheng, son of Prince of Bacheng, was made Prince of Shiping.
idiomatic: His elder brother Prince of Pengcheng Xu was made prince without superior; his younger brother Zizheng, son of Prince of Bacheng, was made prince of Shiping.

literal: Rong was made bearer of the staff of authority, attendant-in-ordinary, commander of all armies at home and abroad, grand general, director of the secretariat, general of the garrison, and commander of the left and right guards; he was enfeoffed as Prince of Taiyuan.
idiomatic: Rong was made bearer of the staff of authority, attendant-in-ordinary, commander of all armies at home and abroad, grand general, director of the secretariat, general of the garrison, and commander of the left and right guards, and enfeoffed as Prince of Taiyuan.

literal: day jihai: the hundred officials in succession, the relevant offices bearing the seal and cord, with the full imperial equipage, welcomed him at the He Bridge.
idiomatic: On jihai day the hundred officials in succession, the relevant offices bearing seal and cord and full imperial equipage, welcomed him at the He Bridge.

literal: day gengzi: the imperial carriage toured the river, west to Taozhu.
idiomatic: On gengzi day the imperial carriage toured the river as far west as Taozhu.

literal: Rong, with military power in his own hands, then harbored a different intent; he killed Empress Dowager Hu and the young sovereign, next killed Prince Without Superior Xu and Prince of Shiping Zizheng, and also killed Chancellor Prince of Gaoyang Yong, Minister of Works Yuan Qin, Palace Attendant of the Third Rank Yuan Hengzhi, Palace Attendant of the Third Rank Prince of Dongping Lue, Prince of Guangping Ti, Prince of Changshan Zhao, Prince of Beiping Chao, Prince of Rencheng Yi, Prince of Zhao Jun Yu, [1] Prince of Zhongshan Shuren, Prince of Qi Commandery Wen, and more than two thousand persons from dukes and ministers downward.
idiomatic: With military power in his own hands Rong then turned traitor: he slew Empress Dowager Hu and the young emperor, then Prince Without Superior Xu and Prince of Shiping Zizheng, then Chancellor Prince of Gaoyang Yong, Minister of Works Yuan Qin, two palace attendants of the third rank—Yuan Hengzhi and Prince of Dongping Lue—and Princes of Guangping, Changshan, Beiping, Rencheng, Zhao, [1] Zhongshan, and Qi Commandery, with more than two thousand from dukes and ministers downward.

literal: Cavalry in ranks guarded the Emperor and moved him to a field pavilion.
idiomatic: Columns of cavalry guarded the emperor and moved him to a field pavilion.

literal: Before long Rong repented and knocked his forehead to the ground in confession.
idiomatic: Soon Rong repented and knocked his forehead to the earth in confession.

literal: The account is in Rong's biography.
idiomatic: The account is in Rong's biography.

literal: day renyin: Prince of Taiyuan Erzhu Rong submitted a memorial asking that Prince Without Superior be posthumously titled emperor.
idiomatic: On renyin day Prince of Taiyuan Erzhu Rong memorialized asking that Prince Without Superior be posthumously titled emperor.

literal: The rest who died at Heyin: princes and regional inspectors were posthumously given the third rank; third-rank officials were given the rank of director; fifth-rank officials were given regional inspector; seventh rank and below were given commandery and garrison posts.
idiomatic: For the rest who died at Heyin: princes and regional inspectors were posthumously given third rank; third-rank officials were given director; fifth-rank, regional inspector; seventh rank and below, commandery and garrison posts.

literal: Descendants of the dead were permitted to establish heirs and were granted titles and fiefs.
idiomatic: Descendants of the dead were allowed to establish heirs and were granted titles and fiefs.

literal: An edict approved it.
idiomatic: An edict approved.

literal: day guimao: the former Minister of Works, Prince of Jiangyang Ji, was made Grand Preceptor and governor of Sizhou;
idiomatic: On guimao day the former minister of works, Prince of Jiangyang Ji, was made grand preceptor and governor of Sizhou;

literal: Grand General of Agile Cavalry, commissioner with credentials, Palace Attendant of the Third Rank, regional inspector of Xiangzhou, Prince of Beihai Hao, was made Grand Tutor and commissioner with credentials, and still regional inspector;
idiomatic: Hao, grand general of agile cavalry, commissioner with credentials, palace attendant of the third rank, regional inspector of Xiang, was made grand tutor and commissioner with credentials, and remained regional inspector;

literal: General Who Pacifies the East, grand master of splendid carriages, Marquis of Qingyuan, state-founding, Li Yanshi, was made Grand Guardian, advanced to Prince of Yangping, and soon transferred to Grand Tutor;
idiomatic: Li Yanshi, general who pacifies the east, grand master of splendid carriages, and state-founding Marquis of Qingyuan, was made grand guardian, advanced to prince of Yangping, and soon transferred to grand tutor;

literal: General Who Pacifies the South, regional inspector of Bingzhou, Yuan Tianmu, was made Minister of Works and enfeoffed as Prince of Shangdang;
idiomatic: Yuan Tianmu, general who pacifies the south and regional inspector of Bing, was made minister of works and enfeoffed Prince of Shangdang;

literal: Attendant-in-ordinary, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Palace Attendant of the Third Rank Yang Chun, was made Minister over the Masses;
idiomatic: Yang Chun, attendant-in-ordinary, grand general of chariots and cavalry, and palace attendant of the third rank, was made minister over the masses;

literal: Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Palace Attendant of the Third Rank, state-founding Duke of Dunqiu Mu Shao, was made Minister of Works, held additionally Director of the Secretariat, and advanced in rank to prince;
idiomatic: Mu Shao, grand general of chariots and cavalry, palace attendant of the third rank, and state-founding Duke of Dunqiu, was made minister of works, held additionally director of the secretariat, and advanced to prince;

literal: Bearer of the staff of authority, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, regional inspector of Yongzhou, Duke of Shangdang Changsun Zhi, was made Grand General of Agile Cavalry, commissioner with credentials of the third rank, advanced in rank to prince, and soon re-enfeoffed as Prince of Fengyi;
idiomatic: Changsun Zhi, bearer of the staff, grand general of chariots and cavalry, regional inspector of Yong, and Duke of Shangdang, was made grand general of agile cavalry with credentials of the third rank, advanced to prince, and soon re-enfeoffed Prince of Fengyi;

literal: General of the central army, Director of the Palace Secretariat Yuan Chen, was made Palace Attendant of the Third Rank and Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, and enfeoffed as Prince of Wei Commandery;
idiomatic: Yuan Chen, general of the central army and director of the palace secretariat, was made palace attendant of the third rank and left vice director of the secretariat, and enfeoffed Prince of Wei Commandery;

literal: General of the central army, Attendant at the Yellow Gate Yuan Xu, was made Prince of the Eastern Sea;
idiomatic: Yuan Xu, general of the central army and attendant at the yellow gate, was made prince of the Eastern Sea;

literal: Grand Master of Splendid Carriages with Golden Seal and Purple Cord, Prince of Guangling Gong, was made Palace Attendant of the Third Rank.
idiomatic: Gong, grand master of splendid carriages with golden seal and purple cord and Prince of Guangling, was made palace attendant of the third rank.

literal: day jiachen: the former titles of the late Prince of Guangyang Yuan and the late Prince of Le'an Jian were restored.
idiomatic: On jiachen day the former titles of the late Prince of Guangyang Yuan and Prince of Le'an Jian were restored.

literal: Palace Attendant of Regular Attendance, Prince of Fucheng Tan, was made Prince of Xianyang; Remonstrator and Critic Yuan Guiping was made Prince of Donglai; Direct Palace Attendant Yuan Su was made Prince of Lu Commandery; Secretariat Gentleman Yuan Ye was made Prince of Changgang; state-founding Duke of Fengyi Yuan Shaojing had his former title of Prince of Longxi restored; state-founding Dukes of Fufeng Feng Tong, Dong Commandery Lu Zizhang, and Beiping Changsun Yue all had their former princely titles restored; because Prince of Beiping Chao was returned, he was again made Prince of Anding.
idiomatic: Tan, palace attendant of regular attendance and Prince of Fucheng, was made Prince of Xianyang; remonstrator Yuan Guiping, Prince of Donglai; direct palace attendant Yuan Su, Prince of Lu; secretariat gentleman Yuan Ye, Prince of Changgang; Yuan Shaojing, state-founding Duke of Fengyi, had his former title Prince of Longxi restored; Feng Tong of Fufeng, Lu Zizhang of Dong, and Changsun Yue of Beiping all had former princely titles restored; Prince of Beiping Chao was again made Prince of Anding.

literal: day dingwei: an edict lifted martial law within and without.
idiomatic: On dingwei day an edict lifted martial law within and without.

literal: day gengxu: Rong's second son Chaluo, grand general, was enfeoffed as Prince of Liang Commandery.
idiomatic: On gengxu day Chaluo, second son of Grand General Erzhu Rong, was enfeoffed Prince of Liang Commandery.

literal: An edict granted the Rouran ruler Anagui the privilege of bowing without being named and of submitting documents without styling himself subject.
idiomatic: An edict granted the Rouran ruler Anagui bowing without being named and memorials without styling himself subject.

literal: That month Prince of Runan Yue, Prince of Beihai Hao, and Prince of Huaiyin Yu in succession fled to Xiao Yan; Regional Inspector of Yingzhou Yuan Yuanda held the south of the city in rebellion.
idiomatic: That month Princes of Runan, Beihai, and Huaiyin fled in succession to Xiao Yan; Yuan Yuanda, regional inspector of Ying, held the south of the city in rebellion.

literal: Fifth month, day dingsi, new moon: Grand General Erzhu Rong was given the additional title of Grand Mobile Circuit of the Northern Route.
idiomatic: On dingsi day, the new moon of the fifth month, Grand General Erzhu Rong was given the additional title of grand mobile circuit of the northern route.

literal: Right Vice Director of the Secretariat Yuan Luo was made envoy of the eastern circuit; General Who Campaigns East Yuan Xin was made his deputy; they toured the regions for promotion and demotion, acting first and reporting afterward.
idiomatic: Yuan Luo, right vice director of the secretariat, was made envoy of the eastern circuit; Yuan Xin, general who campaigns east, was deputy; they toured the regions for promotion and demotion, acting first and reporting afterward.

literal: day xinyou: Grand General Erzhu Rong returned to Jinyang; the Emperor saw him off on the north slope of Mount Mang.
idiomatic: On xinyou day Grand General Erzhu Rong returned to Jinyang; the emperor saw him off on the north slope of Mount Mang.

literal: day bingyin: an edict said: "Since the late Xiaochang era laws and orders have grown dim; those who kept faith and plain integrity found no way to declare themselves; long-held grievances had nowhere to plead.
idiomatic: On bingyin day an edict said: "Since the late Xiaochang era laws and orders have grown dim; those who kept faith and plain integrity found no way to be heard; long-held grievances had nowhere to plead.

literal: Those whose affairs lie on the public road yet were wrongly suspected, whose cases under statute were without fault yet were wrongly suppressed, or who suffered unfair selection or onerous levies and corvée—such cases are too many to list.
idiomatic: Those whose affairs belong on the public road yet were wrongly suspected, whose cases under statute were without fault yet were wrongly suppressed, or who suffered unfair selection or onerous levies and corvée—such cases are beyond counting.

literal: Those whose petitions through the imperial coach office do not conform to procedure shall all assemble at the east gate of Hualin; We shall personally judge wrongful cases to clear accumulated wrongs.
idiomatic: Those whose petitions through the imperial coach office do not conform to procedure shall all assemble at the east gate of Hualin; we shall personally judge wrongful cases to clear accumulated wrongs.

literal: " day jisi: the people of Qi province, Jia Hao, gathered a host in rebellion, raided the provincial city by night, and at dawn withdrew.
idiomatic: " On jisi day Jia Hao of Qi province gathered a host in rebellion, raided the provincial city by night, and withdrew at dawn.

literal: day yihai: Regional Inspector of Jinzhou Fan Zihu took Tangzhou, beheaded Regional Inspector Cui Yuanzhen and Mobile-Circuit Attendant Li Yun, and sent their heads to the capital.
idiomatic: On yihai day Fan Zihu, regional inspector of Jin, took Tangzhou, beheaded regional inspector Cui Yuanzhen and mobile-circuit attendant Li Yun, and sent their heads to the capital.

literal: day renwu: an edict sought men of virtue, literary accomplishment, and upright governance; magistrates, regional inspectors, and governors were all to set forth their aims and achievements in full memorial.
idiomatic: On renwu day an edict sought men of virtue, literary accomplishment, and upright governance; magistrates, governors, and regional inspectors were to set forth aims and achievements in full memorial.

literal: When three or more were obtained, the magistrate, governor, or regional inspector was rewarded one rank;
idiomatic: When three or more worthy men were found, the magistrate, governor, or regional inspector was rewarded one rank;

literal: if the men recommended were unfit, one rank was also demoted.
idiomatic: if the men recommended were unfit, one rank was likewise demoted.

literal: It was also ordered that in the old system military merit ranks did not exceed General Who Campaigns Abroad; from now on they should follow the former pattern upward, with remaining ranks accumulating into grade.
idiomatic: It was also ordered that under the old system military merit ranks did not exceed general who campaigns abroad; from now on they should follow the former pattern upward, with remaining ranks accumulating into grade.

literal: Those who had followed the imperial carriage north were not in this category.
idiomatic: Those who had followed the imperial carriage north were excepted.

literal: All were forbidden to break grade to receive rank; breaking rank was to request silk instead.
idiomatic: All were forbidden to break grade to receive rank; breaking rank meant requesting silk instead.

literal: Earlier Xiao Yan had sent his general Cao Yizong to raid Jingzhou.
idiomatic: Earlier Xiao Yan had sent his general Cao Yizong to raid Jing.

literal: day guimao: General of the central army and Director of the Ministry of Personnel Fei Mu was made bearer of the staff of authority and commander of the southern campaign armies, directing Regional Inspector of Jing Wang Pi to attack him.
idiomatic: On guimao day Fei Mu, general of the central army and director of the ministry of personnel, was made bearer of the staff and commander of the southern campaign armies, directing Wang Pi, regional inspector of Jing, to attack him.

literal: Sixth month, day dinghai, new moon: the Emperor's elder brother, state-founding Duke of Zhending Zhi, was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Chenliu.
idiomatic: On dinghai day, the new moon of the sixth month, the emperor's elder brother Zhi, state-founding Duke of Zhending, was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Chenliu.

literal: day gengyin: General Who Guards the Army, Grand Master of Splendid Carriages Li Qian, was made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Palace Attendant of the Third Rank, and specially advanced.
idiomatic: On gengyin day Li Qian, general who guards the army and grand master of splendid carriages, was made grand general of chariots and cavalry, palace attendant of the third rank, and specially advanced.

literal: day xinmao: Regional Inspector of Southern Jing Li Zhi held the south of the city in rebellion.
idiomatic: On xinmao day Li Zhi, regional inspector of southern Jing, held the south of the city in rebellion.

literal: Palace Attendant of Regular Attendance Gao Qianyou and his brothers led gathered refugees and raised troops on the plain of Qi province, repeatedly defeating provincial troops; the eastern-circuit envoy Yuan Xin conveyed the imperial intent, and they surrendered.
idiomatic: Gao Qianyou, palace attendant of regular attendance, and his brothers led gathered refugees and raised troops on the plain of Qi, repeatedly defeating provincial troops; eastern-circuit envoy Yuan Xin conveyed the imperial intent, and they surrendered.

literal: That month Ge Rong, in famine, had his vice director Ren Bao lead more than thirty thousand carts south in raid, reaching Qin River.
idiomatic: That month Ge Rong, starving, had his vice director Ren Bao lead more than thirty thousand carts south in raid as far as Qin River.

literal: day guimao: the heir of the King of Gaochang, Guang, was made General Who Pacifies the West and regional inspector of Guazhou, inheriting the title state-founding Marquis of Tailin, [2] King of Gaochang.
idiomatic: On guimao day Guang, heir of the King of Gaochang, was made general who pacifies the west and regional inspector of Gua, inheriting the title state-founding Marquis of Tailin, [2] King of Gaochang.

literal: Minister of Works, Prince of Shangdang Tianmu, was made grand commander of the northeastern-route armies, leading Commandant of the Imperial Clan Zhensun, Xi Yi, Heba Sheng, Erzhu Yangdu, and others to attack Ren Bao.
idiomatic: Tianmu, minister of works and Prince of Shangdang, was made grand commander of the northeastern-route armies, leading Zhensun, commandant of the imperial clan, Xi Yi, Heba Sheng, Erzhu Yangdu, and others against Ren Bao.

literal: The Emperor, because bandit troubles were not yet settled, avoided the main hall, blamed himself, and withdrew delicacies.
idiomatic: Because bandit troubles were not yet settled, the emperor avoided the main hall, blamed himself, and withdrew delicacies.

literal: Recruitment placards were also posted to gather the loyal and brave.
idiomatic: Recruitment placards were also posted to gather the loyal and brave.

literal: Those who offered straight counsel, men daring to die for righteousness, plans touching the state's gain and harm, or conduct answering peril to ruler and kin were to assemble at Hualin Park and discuss affairs face to face.
idiomatic: Men of straight counsel, those ready to die for righteousness, advisers on the state's gain and harm, or anyone answering peril to ruler and kin were to gather at Hualin Park and speak with the throne face to face.

literal: Xing Shuo, chief clerk of the Pingbei office in Youzhou, led more than a hundred thousand households of refugees from Hebei in rebellion at Beihai in Qingzhou, styled himself King of Han, and adopted the era name Tiantong.
idiomatic: Xing Shuo, chief clerk of the Pingbei office in You, led more than a hundred thousand households of refugees from Hebei in rebellion at Beihai in Qing, styled himself King of Han, and adopted the era name Tiantong.

literal: day wushen: General Who Campaigns East, Grand Master of Splendid Carriages Li Shuren, was made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Palace Attendant of the Third Rank, and led troops to attack him.
idiomatic: On wushen day Li Shuren, general who campaigns east and grand master of splendid carriages, was made grand general of chariots and cavalry, palace attendant of the third rank, and led troops against him.

literal: An edict ordered Direct Attendant Ji Ye, bearer of the staff, to recruit newly released pasture households; those who enrolled to serve were given ninth-rank office.
idiomatic: An edict ordered Ji Ye, direct attendant and bearer of the staff, to recruit newly released pasture households; those who enrolled to serve were given ninth-rank office.

literal: day jiyou: an edict said that those with private horses and arms who followed the campaign, if officeholders, received preferential advancement of two major ranks and also substantive office;
idiomatic: On jiyou day an edict said that those with private horses and arms who followed the campaign, if officeholders, received preferential advancement of two major ranks and also substantive office;

literal: if commoners entering service, preferential advancement of two ranks outside the register and also substantive office.
idiomatic: commoners entering service received two preferential ranks beyond the register and substantive office as well.

literal: If martial skill surpassed the norm, even without a private horse the previous article applied;
idiomatic: If martial skill surpassed the norm, even without a private horse the same rule applied;

literal: even if not surpassing the norm, but skilled in one art such as shooting the lance or lifting the bar and showing some mettle in courage and strategy, beyond rank by sequence one major rank was specially granted preferentially and substantive office given.
idiomatic: if not surpassing the norm but skilled in one art—shooting the lance or lifting the bar—and showing courage and plan, beyond sequence one major rank was specially added and substantive office granted.

literal: If there was no surname rank, entry was from the eighth rank, ranks added as before, and substantive office specially granted.
idiomatic: Without a surname rank, entry began at the eighth rank, ranks were added as above, and substantive office was specially granted.

literal: day xinhai: an edict said: "We shall personally lead the six armies, sweep and settle Yan and Dai; Grand General, Prince of Taiyuan Erzhu Rong shall lead a hundred thousand picked troops as the left army; Prince of Shangdang Tianmu shall command eighty thousand as the vanguard; Minister over the Masses Yang Chun shall marshal a hundred thousand as the right army; Minister of Works Mu Shao shall command eighty thousand as the rear army."
idiomatic: On xinhai day an edict said: "We shall personally lead the six armies and sweep Yan and Dai; Grand General Prince of Taiyuan Erzhu Rong shall lead a hundred thousand picked troops as the left army; Prince of Shangdang Tianmu eighty thousand as the vanguard; Minister over the Masses Yang Chun a hundred thousand as the right army; Minister of Works Mu Shao eighty thousand as the rear army."

literal: That month Ge Rong's host withdrew and encamped north of Xiangzhou.
idiomatic: That month Ge Rong's host withdrew and encamped north of Xiang.

literal: Seventh month of autumn, day dingsi: an edict said that from the fourth rank upward those who followed the campaign might not receive preferential rank; those of the regular fourth rank received one preferential rank.
idiomatic: On dingsi day in the seventh month of autumn an edict said that from the fourth rank upward those who followed the campaign might not receive preferential rank; those of the regular fourth rank received one preferential rank.

literal: In military grade from the third rank upward, if they followed the campaign, fourth-rank officials received one major preferential rank.
idiomatic: By military grade, from the third rank up those who joined the campaign gave fourth-rank men one major preferential step.

literal: [3] From the regular fifth rank downward, the former rules still applied; if campaign ranks totaled more than ten, they were counted into the fourth or third rank.
idiomatic: [3] For the regular fifth rank and below the old rules still held; when campaign ranks exceeded ten in total, they were folded into the fourth or third rank.

literal: Award was limited to five ranks.
idiomatic: Award was limited to five ranks.

literal: day jiwei: an edict made Tang Jingxuan, former provisional administrator of Dong Commandery, bearer of the staff and commander, to recruit two thousand sojourning refugees in Dong Commandery, cross the river and build stockades as convenient, and align with the imperial army.
idiomatic: On jiwei day an edict made Tang Jingxuan, former provisional administrator of Dong, bearer of the staff and commander, to recruit two thousand sojourning refugees in Dong Commandery, cross the river and build stockades as convenient, and align with the imperial army.

literal: That month Qi Xianwu Wang northwest of Ye comforted and instructed seven of Ge Rong's detached chiefs who styled themselves kings, more than ten thousand in all, and they surrendered.
idiomatic: That month Qi Xianwu Wang northwest of Ye comforted and instructed seven of Ge Rong's detached chiefs who styled themselves kings—more than ten thousand in all—and they surrendered.

literal: day yichou: Grand General Erzhu Rong was given the additional titles of Pillar Grand General and recorder of Secretariat affairs.
idiomatic: On yichou day Grand General Erzhu Rong was given the additional titles of pillar grand general and recorder of secretariat affairs.

literal: day xinsi: the Secretariat memorialized cutting off the public provision of robes, caps, swords, girdles, and shoes for the hundred officials.
idiomatic: On xinsi day the secretariat memorialized cutting off the public provision of robes, caps, swords, girdles, and shoes for the hundred officials.

literal: day renzi: Liu Ju of Guang province gathered several thousand in rebellion at Puyang and styled himself Grand General Huangwu.
idiomatic: On renzi day Liu Ju of Guang province gathered several thousand in rebellion at Puyang and styled himself Grand General Huangwu.

literal: That month a man of Gaoping garrison, Moqi Chounu, usurped the great position and installed the hundred offices.
idiomatic: That month Moqi Chounu of Gaoping garrison usurped the great position and installed the hundred offices.

literal: That month, [4] Prince of Huaiyin Yu returned to court from the south.
idiomatic: That month [4] Prince of Huaiyin Yu came back to court from the south.

literal: Eighth month: Yang Kan, administrator of Taishan, held the commandery and brought in Xiao Yan's general Wang Bian to attack Yanzhou.
idiomatic: In the eighth month Yang Kan, administrator of Tai, held the commandery and brought in Xiao Yan's general Wang Bian to attack Yan.

literal: [5] day jiachen: an edict ordered Grand Commander Zhensun, commandant of the imperial clan, to lead Regional Inspector of Southern Guang Zheng Xianhu to attack Liu Ju at Puyang; he was defeated and pacified.
idiomatic: [5] On jiachen day an edict ordered Grand Commander Zhensun, commandant of the imperial clan, to lead Zheng Xianhu, regional inspector of southern Guang, to attack Liu Ju at Puyang; he was defeated and pacified.

literal: Attendant-in-ordinary, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Prince of Huaiyin Yu, was made Palace Attendant of the Third Rank.
idiomatic: Yu, attendant-in-ordinary, grand general of agile cavalry, and Prince of Huaiyin, was made palace attendant of the third rank.

literal: That month Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Palace Attendant of the Third Rank Li Shuren attacked Xing Shuo on the Wei River, was defeated, and returned.
idiomatic: That month Li Shuren, grand general of chariots and cavalry and palace attendant of the third rank, attacked Xing Shuo on the Wei River, was defeated, and returned.

literal: Grand Commander Fei Mu greatly defeated Xiao Yan's army, captured his general Cao Yizong, and sent him caged to the capital.
idiomatic: Grand Commander Fei Mu routed Xiao Yan's forces, took his general Cao Yizong, and sent him to the capital in a cage.

literal: Xiao Yan made Prince of Beihai Hao ruler of Wei, era name Xiaoji, and he entered and held Qiaocheng in southern Yan.
idiomatic: Xiao Yan made Prince of Beihai Hao ruler of Wei, era name Xiaoji; he entered and held Qiaocheng in southern Yan.

literal: Eleventh month, day wuwu: the heir of Prince Without Superior Shao was made Prince of Pengcheng; Zikuan, son of Prince of Chenliu, was made Prince of Chenliu; his younger brother Gang was made Prince of Fuyang; Gang's younger brother Zhi was made Prince of Linlu.
idiomatic: On wuwu day in the eleventh month the heir of Prince Without Superior Shao was made Prince of Pengcheng; Zikuan, son of Prince of Chenliu, Prince of Chenliu; his younger brother Gang, Prince of Fuyang; Gang's younger brother Zhi, Prince of Linlu.

literal: day guihai: Qi Xianwu Wang and Mobile-Circuit Attendant Yu Hui, with the Xu-Yan mobile circuit Yu Xiaofen and Grand Commander Diao Xuan, greatly defeated Yang Kan at Xiaqiu; Kan fled to Xiao Yan.
idiomatic: On guihai day Qi Xianwu Wang and mobile-circuit attendant Yu Hui, with the Xu-Yan mobile circuit Yu Xiaofen and Grand Commander Diao Xuan, greatly defeated Yang Kan at Xiaqiu; Kan fled to Xiao Yan.

literal: Yanzhou was pacified.
idiomatic: Yan was pacified.

literal: day wuyin: Prince of Shangdang Tianmu was made grand general and commissioner with credentials, with hereditary regional inspector of Bing.
idiomatic: On wuyin day Prince of Shangdang Tianmu was made grand general and commissioner with credentials, with hereditary regional inspector of Bing.

literal: Former General, Grand Master of the Palace Yuan Ning was enfeoffed as Prince of Dong'an.
idiomatic: Yuan Ning, former general and grand master of the palace, was enfeoffed Prince of Dong'an.
